cells.tense: You are letting go of what is done, and doing it on purpose.
cells.ask: Name one thing you finished, out loud, once, and do nothing else with it today.
cells.core:
Something you tended has come in. Not everything you planted, not the parts that failed — but a piece of the work is finished, done, and you are letting it be that.

The end of it does not land as loss. That is the unusual part. You can put down the thing you carried for a long time without calling yourself defeated, and the space it leaves is space you chose. Days from now, when something new asks for your hands, there will be room. Keep releasing at the rate the season actually ends — not faster to be generous, not slower out of fear — and say plainly that you finished it. Release only holds when you have claimed what it came from.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it, and you can set it down without calling it a loss.
cells.place: where you let go of what's finished

cells.tense: You are bracing for what comes after this, before you have let the old one end.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are done with and do nothing further with it — no improving, no reviving, no defending — for one full day.
cells.core:
A harvest is here, and you are already at the next planting. Something that took a long time is standing in front of you, and instead of putting anything down, you are reaching forward — how to keep this, how to top it, what happens when it goes.

Keeping a hand on the thing crowds what grew. Letting it end for real feels like losing it, so nothing gets to finish, and nothing gets to start. None of this asks you to care less. Ease in the middle of abundance is a different thing from vigilance — it is what makes the next stretch livable instead of another thing to guard. Notice what you reach for before the season is over, and let one grip stay open.
cells.sheetLine: You have the harvest and you are too braced to set anything down.
cells.place: where you let go of what's finished

cells.tense: You stopped letting things end, and you have been standing there ever since.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you are still holding that is actually over, then put the page somewhere you will not look today.
cells.core:
There is a harvest you are not standing in. Letting go did not land the way it was supposed to, or nobody was there to see it, so you stopped letting things end and you started keeping them.

You cannot start anything new with your hands full of things that already finished, and you cannot rest inside what you grew, because resting means admitting it is done. What is missing is not ability. It is the choice of where to point next, and that choice is yours alone to make. Pick one direction, small, go there, and let the next season arrive on its own. Nothing has to be carried that is already over.
cells.sheetLine: You are still holding things that already ended.

cells.tense: You are already letting things end, and calling it something that happened to you.
cells.ask: Call one finished thing finished in front of someone who watched you grow it.
cells.core:
You let go of something recently, maybe more than one thing. Backed off a project, stopped pushing someone, set down a role you had carried — and the way you tell it, the situation changed or the timing passed.

It was not the timing. You finished it, on purpose, and where you are standing came from that. Not calling it yours means you cannot tell whether you were right, and cannot do it again without waiting for circumstances to move first. The release is already working. What is missing is the credit — one sentence out loud, from the person it belongs to, about what they let go. Say it. Somebody watches you to learn how endings go, and right now they are learning that things end by themselves.
cells.sheetLine: You already let it go. You are just calling it circumstance.
cells.place: where you let go of what's finished
